channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Uzbek President Oversees Preparations for Major International Events in Bukhara
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev held a meeting on preparations for major international events in Bukhara. He stressed the need for comprehensive development of transport, services, security, and urban infrastructure, not just event venues. The focus is on a holistic approach to ensure successful events.

item.title: Kazakhstan Police Seize Over Two Thousand Firearms Since Year Start
item.description: Since the beginning of the year, Kazakh police have confiscated over two thousand firearms from illegal circulation. This includes 184 criminal weapons and 160 weapons stolen during the January events. A recent operation in October yielded over 170 firearms and 800 ammunition rounds.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Register Citizens Traveling Abroad for Work to Prevent Sex Trafficking
item.description: Kazakhstan is strengthening its fight against human trafficking with a new plan for 2027-2029. The government will monitor suspicious job postings online and create a registry for private employment agencies. Citizens traveling abroad for work will be registered to better track exploitation risks.

item.title: Uzbek President Launches 55 Projects and Initiates Construction of 90 More in Bukhara
item.description: During his visit to Bukhara, President Shavkat Mirziyoyev participated in a ceremony to launch 55 new projects and start the construction of 90 others. These projects, valued at $7.8 billion, span various sectors including energy, manufacturing, agriculture, and tourism, aiming to boost production and exports.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Dollar Exchange Rate Decreases for Third Consecutive Day
item.description: The dollar exchange rate in Uzbekistan has fallen for the third day in a row. The Central Bank announced the official exchange rates for foreign currencies against the Uzbek soum, effective November 4th. This marks a continued trend of depreciation for the US dollar.

item.title: Kazakhstan Secures $1.3 Billion in Investment for Alatau City Development
item.description: Kazakhstan has signed nine international agreements in London to develop Alatau City, with an estimated investment potential of $1.3 billion. The deals focus on infrastructure, education, and healthcare. The agreements were finalized at the Alatau City Investment Roundtable, marking the start of Kazakhstan's European investment tour.

item.title: Trump and Taliban Leader Share Similarities in Restricting Media Freedom
item.description: Donald Trump and Taliban Supreme Leader Mullah Hibatullah Akhundzada, listed by Reporters Without Borders for restricting media freedom, share a hostile approach to dissent and independent media. Both leaders undermine press credibility and present themselves as figures beyond criticism, despite differing political systems.

item.title: Almaty Bus Operators Face Service Cuts Amid 15 Billion Tenge Subsidy Debt
item.description: Almaty's public transport operators are threatening to reduce bus services starting November 2nd due to an accumulated subsidy debt exceeding 15 billion tenge. City authorities stated the debt repayment will be considered during budget finalization. A social media user criticized the city's statement blaming passengers for overcrowding, highlighting the financial strain on transport companies.

item.title: A Woman's Account of Life and Abuse in Taliban Prisons
item.description: This article provides a firsthand account of the experiences of women and girls imprisoned by the Taliban in Afghanistan over the past five years. Many are jailed without proof of crime, facing vague accusations or issues related to family and social pressures. The author shares personal observations and stories heard from fellow inmates, detailing prison life and treatment.

item.title: Uzbekistan President Launches 145 Projects Worth $7.8 Billion in Bukhara
item.description: The President of Uzbekistan has initiated the launch and construction of 145 projects valued at $7.8 billion in Bukhara. These projects span various sectors including petrochemicals, textiles, energy, construction, industry, agriculture, tourism, infrastructure, and services.

item.title: Almaty Heating Bills to Show Heat Consumption in Gigacalories from November 2026
item.description: Starting November 2026, Almaty heating bills will display heat consumption in gigacalories instead of the amount in tenge per square meter. 'Almaty Thermal Networks' explained that the tariff is already set per gigacalorie, but bills will now show actual consumption and the tariff per unit.

item.title: Kazakhstan and Azerbaijan Plan to Build New Ferry System
item.description: Kazakhstan and Azerbaijan intend to construct a new ferry system. This initiative aims to enhance transportation links and trade between the two countries.

item.title: Kazakhstan Streamlines Drug Registration for US and European Medicines
item.description: Kazakhstan has simplified the registration process for medicines produced in the USA and Europe, reducing the time to 15 working days. The Ministry of Health announced that this change, effective from 2026, consolidates expertise, registration, and price regulation into a single 'one-stop-shop' service. Sixteen medicines and medical devices have already been registered under this accelerated procedure.

item.title: Kyrgyz President Orders Review of Farmer Access to Preferential Loans
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov has ordered an investigation into whether farmers in Kyrgyzstan are receiving preferential loans at reduced rates. The issue was raised by farmers concerned about high interest rates, with one reporting paying 20-22% annually.

item.title: Kazakhstan and India Sign Extradition Treaty for Wanted Individuals
item.description: Kazakhstan and India have signed an agreement on the extradition of individuals wanted by law enforcement agencies. The treaty was signed by Kazakhstan's Prosecutor General Berik Asylov and India's Ambassador to Kazakhstan, Silas Tangal. This agreement will allow both countries to hand over wanted persons for criminal prosecution or to serve sentences.

item.title: Kazakh President Criticizes Road Conditions, 33 Investigations Launched
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has criticized the state of roads. Prosecutors have identified violations totaling 8 billion tenge in damages, leading to 33 investigations. Contracts and public procurement plans worth 36 billion tenge have been canceled.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Disclose Insurance Agent Commission Amounts
item.description: The amount of commission remuneration for insurance agents in Kazakhstan will no longer be a secret. New regulations aim to increase transparency in the insurance sector. This change is expected to impact how agents are compensated and how consumers perceive insurance products.

item.title: Gasoline and Diesel Prices Surge in Astana
item.description: Prices for AI-92 gasoline and diesel fuel have sharply increased in Astana. AI-92 gasoline rose by eight tenge per liter at some major gas station networks, reaching 261 tenge. This marks the most significant single price increase since the beginning of 2025. AI-95 gasoline and diesel fuel also saw price hikes.

item.title: Almaty Residents to See New Heating Bill Format from November
item.description: Starting in November, Almaty residents will see a new format for heating charges on their utility bills. Instead of a price per square meter, bills will display the amount of heat consumed in gigacalories (Gcal). This change aims to make charges clearer, showing the volume of heat and the tariff per Gcal.

item.title: Budget Funds for Road Repair Embezzled in Akmola Region
item.description: Budget funds allocated for road repair have been embezzled in the Akmola region. The specific details of the embezzlement and the amount of funds involved have not yet been disclosed. Investigations into the matter are likely underway.

item.title: Kazakhstan Releases Second Amur Tiger into the Wild for Restoration Program
item.description: Kazakhstan has released a second Amur tiger, named Amur, into the Ile-Balkhash State Nature Reserve as part of a program to reintroduce the species. The first tiger, Umit, released in July, is reportedly hunting independently. Tigers were extinct in Kazakhstan by the mid-20th century.

item.title: Kazakhstan aims to become Central Asia's digital hub with data centers
item.description: Kazakhstan plans to develop large data processing centers, aiming to become a key digital hub in Central Asia. The Data Center Valley project in Ekibastuz targets 1 GW capacity. Experts question the economic benefits beyond infrastructure rental.

item.title: Uzbekistan to raise liquefied gas price for population by 2.5 times from November 15
item.description: From November 15, Uzbekistan will increase the retail price of liquefied gas for the population by 2.5 times, from 2,000 to 5,000 Uzbek soums per kilogram. The new price includes VAT. Compensations will be provided for low-income families.

item.title: Taliban Governor Accused of Appointing Relatives and Allies in Parwan Province
item.description: Local sources in Parwan province report that Taliban governor Azizurrahman Mansoor has dismissed officials and appointed friends and family to key positions. An attempt to appoint his son-in-law led to an armed clash, wounding six fighters. Institutions are reportedly treated as 'spoils of war,' with experienced staff being removed.

item.title: Kazakhstan Reports Nearly 50 Cases of Assault or Threats Against Medical Workers Since April
item.description: Nearly 50 cases of threats or physical assault against medical workers have been registered in Kazakhstan since April, according to Health Minister Akmaral Alnazarova. The announcement followed an incident in Aktau where a patient's father allegedly assaulted a doctor. A new article in the criminal code specifically addresses such offenses.

item.title: Kazakh Party "Adilet" Launches Project for Legal Aid and Rights Protection
item.description: The "Adilet" party has launched a project called "Adilet Ortasy" to help citizens protect their rights and businesses resolve legal disputes. The initiative will offer free consultations, simplify legal language, and establish a contact center to address systemic issues identified through eOtinish and social media.

item.title: First Phase of Large Solar Power Station in Jeyhun Nearing Completion
item.description: Construction of the 250 MW 'Jeyhun' solar power station in Tajikistan's Jeyhun district is progressing. The first phase includes a 220 kV substation and eight photovoltaic sites totaling 50 MW. Over 95% of concrete work for the substation is done, with building construction and equipment installation underway. The project aims to boost Tajikistan's power generation and renewable energy use.

item.title: School Supplies Shortage Worsens Amid Economic Crisis in Turkmenistan
item.description: Amid Turkmenistan's deepening economic crisis, school supply issues are intensifying, with schools increasingly relying on parental contributions. Reports indicate teachers are asking parents to create funds for school necessities. While Turkmen law guarantees free education, schools have been continuously collecting money from parents for expenses over the past decades. Authorities rarely acknowledge these issues.

item.title: Almaty Hosts Discussions on President Tokayev's Address, Attracting 2,500 Participants
item.description: Approximately 2,500 people participated in a series of meetings in Almaty to discuss President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev's address, "Kazakhstan's Current Challenges in a New Historical Cycle." The events, held across all city districts, included representatives from various sectors. The goal was to gather citizen proposals for state-level consideration.

item.title: Uzbekistan Increases Base Electricity Tariff to 350 kWh for Unheated Areas
item.description: Uzbekistan has increased the base monthly electricity consumption tariff to 350 kWh for areas without natural gas supply during the heating season. This change, effective November 1, 2026, aims to support the population during the transition to market principles in the energy sector. The standard base rate remains 200 kWh.

item.title: Kazakhstan Changes Rules for Managing Pension Fund Assets
item.description: Kazakhstan has updated regulations allowing individuals to divide their pension savings among multiple investment portfolios and private management companies. Savers can now allocate up to 100% of their funds to private management, offering greater choice in investment strategies.

item.title: Criminal Case Opened After Mass Food Poisoning of Kazakh Footballers in Tashkent
item.description: A criminal case has been initiated in Tashkent following a mass food poisoning incident involving young Kazakh footballers and their chaperones. Twenty individuals required medical attention after falling ill during a tournament.

item.title: Tajik President Emomali Rahmon Inspects Development Projects in Sughd Region
item.description: Tajik President Emomali Rahmon is on a working visit to the Sughd region. During his trip, he inaugurated new enterprises and a hotel, and reviewed plans for road and bridge construction. The president's visit to the region is ongoing.

item.title: UN Envoy Rabab Fatima Visits Torkham Maternity Unit, Stresses Healthcare Needs
item.description: Rabab Fatima, UN Special Representative for Afghanistan, visited the maternity emergency unit at Omari Camp in Torkham. She emphasized the need to expand essential healthcare services for mothers and reaffirmed support for providing psychosocial services to returning women and girls, particularly mothers and pregnant women.

item.title: Bishkek Considers Hiring Foreigners as Bus Drivers Amid Shortage
item.description: Bishkek's municipal transport enterprise is exploring the possibility of hiring foreign nationals as bus drivers to address a shortage. While local drivers are still preferred, the initiative, framed as labor migration, suggests foreign drivers would need basic language skills for route identification. The situation is still under review.

item.title: Kazakhstan and China Consider $200 Million Fund for Middle Corridor Transport Route
item.description: Kazakhstan and China are discussing a joint investment fund, potentially reaching $200 million, to develop the Trans-Caspian International Transport Route. This route, also known as the Middle Corridor, links China and Europe via Kazakhstan and the Caspian Sea. The fund was proposed by Kazakhstan in July and involves potential participants like Baiterek National Investment Holding and China's Silk Road Fund.

item.title: Another Tajik Citizen Buried After Dying in War in Ukraine
item.description: Dilovar Jafoev, a 41-year-old Tajik citizen, has been buried in Khorog, Gorno-Badakhshan Autonomous Region, after dying in Russia's war against Ukraine. He had been living and working in Russia for about a year before signing a contract with the Russian Ministry of Defense. His exact circumstances of death remain unknown.

item.title: 12 Dead from Gas Poisoning in Fergana Valley in Two Days; Emergency Services Warn of Unsafe Boilers
item.description: Twelve people have died from carbon monoxide poisoning in Uzbekistan's Fergana region within two days. The Emergency Situations Directorate attributed the tragedies to severe safety violations in gas heating systems, particularly with old, illegally modified boilers.

item.title: Afghanistan and Russia Hold Economic Cooperation Meeting in Kabul
item.description: A coordination meeting on economic cooperation between Afghanistan and the Russian Federation took place in Kabul. The meeting was chaired by Mullah Abdul Ghani Baradar, Deputy Prime Minister for Economic Affairs. The Ministry of Finance presented a report during the session.

item.title: Large Agro-Industrial Complex to Be Built in Jizzakh, Uzbekistan
item.description: A $140 million investment project is planned for Jizzakh, Uzbekistan, focusing on agricultural product processing, water-saving technologies, and new production facilities. The project aims to create employment for a thousand citizens and involves partnerships with Chinese companies.
